a2-ss6: Overstimulating also dehydrates them, but we can't give fluids unless they're fully alert, able to swallow and not vomiting, and then just small sips of an electrolyte drink. If they still show the signs of low electrolytes from MDMA: Magnesium Alarm above, they may need more salt, potassium and magnesium than a normal electrolyte drink has. Salty potato chips give the salt and the potassium with nothing to cook, so I'd let them eat as many as they want. That's the only way I'd give potassium, since too much pure potassium is dangerous for anyone. Their potassium could be running high as well as low, though: MDMA can drain it, but muscles breaking down into the blood push it up. High potassium also brings on vomiting and diarrhea, which then drain it again, so if those start, I'd stop the chips. Magnesium also runs low in many people with serotonin syndrome (a nursing review). Magnesium chloride tastes too bad for most people to drink, but the skin absorbs it, so I'd stir a handful of magnesium chloride flakes into a little water and rub the mix on their skin. If you don't have the flakes, Epsom salt, which is magnesium sulfate rather than a kind of table salt, works the same way, just less well. If they can stand the taste, they can also take magnesium chloride by mouth, especially with MDMA-related jaw tension or twitching (the amounts are in MDMA: Magnesium Alarm, above).
a2-ss8: Since a seizure is one of the main dangers while you wait, I'd use DMSO, which seems to help prevent them, going by people's reports rather than studies: at any sign of an overdose, have them smell it or rub a little on a clean patch of skin (with 30% water if the skin itches), then use a little more at a time, since some people react more strongly than others. You might also think of niacin, which this guide uses for ending a trip, but it's unsafe with serotonin syndrome, since at the doses used to end a trip it can cause flushing and low blood pressure (NIH). The other remedy I'd keep for a last resort, if nothing else is helping and no medics are coming, is Syrian rue oil, since it makes trips, ayahuasca included, much less intense. The oil isn't the Syrian rue brew from step 1, which blocks MAO and is dangerous with MDMA for that reason, but nobody has studied the oil with MDMA either.
a2-mdma: Once their jaw tenses, that should be their last dose of MDMA, so get them to slow down and cool off. While it's natural to want to dance on MDMA, I'd tell everyone not to dance at all, since dancing makes the heat and the sweat that drain their salt. If they drink a lot of plain water, even a single normal MDMA dose raises the risk of their sodium dropping too low, so have them sip an electrolyte drink when they're thirsty instead. Plain water is the risk because MDMA makes the body hold on to water, which thins out the salt left in their blood, all the more after they've sweated a lot. The following indicators would justify calling medics: If their confusion or headache worsens, or vomiting won't stop (sodium might be too low by then for an electrolyte drink to fix; while you wait for medics, if they're alert and not vomiting, give them something very salty instead, like strong broth). That has to be a lot of salt, more than a snack gives: guidelines for hikers who drank too much water use three or four bouillon cubes in half a cup of water. If their muscles keep getting weaker or their heart palpitations keep getting stronger, that could be from dangerously low potassium, like my second wife had. A seizure or collapse can result from low sodium, magnesium or potassium, and can also come from overheating or MDMA toxicity.
